specs.title: NIP-01: Basic protocol flow description
specs.summary: The core protocol: the event object, how its id and signature are computed, what makes a kind regular, replaceable or addressable, and the messages clients and relays exchange.

specs.title: NIP-02: Follow List
specs.summary: Kind 3, the follow list: one p tag per followed key, each carrying an optional relay hint and petname.

specs.title: NIP-03: OpenTimestamps Attestations for Events
specs.summary: Kind 1040, which carries an OpenTimestamps proof that another event existed before a given Bitcoin block.

specs.title: NIP-04: Encrypted Direct Message
specs.summary: Kind 4, encrypted direct messages built on a shared secret and aes-256-cbc, superseded by NIP-17.

specs.title: NIP-05: Mapping Nostr keys to DNS-based internet identifiers
specs.summary: How a key claims an email-like address, by serving a nostr.json document under the domain that maps a name to that pubkey.

specs.title: NIP-06: Basic key derivation from mnemonic seed phrase
specs.summary: Deriving a key from a BIP39 mnemonic along the m/44'/1237' path.

specs.title: NIP-07: `window.nostr` capability for web browsers
specs.summary: The window.nostr object a browser extension exposes, letting a web page read a public key and have events signed without ever seeing the private key.

specs.title: NIP-08: Handling Mentions
specs.summary: The old #[index] notation for mentioning events and pubkeys inside a note, replaced by NIP-27.

specs.title: NIP-09: Event Deletion Request
specs.summary: Kind 5, the deletion request, where an author asks relays to drop events they signed earlier.

specs.title: NIP-10: Text Notes and Threads
specs.summary: How kind 1 notes thread: the markers on e tags that name the root and the parent, and the q tags that cite another event.

specs.title: NIP-11: Relay Information Document
specs.summary: The JSON document a relay serves over HTTP to describe itself: its name, its contacts, the NIPs it supports, its limits and its policies.

specs.title: NIP-13: Proof of Work
specs.summary: Proof of work over an event id, mined with a nonce tag and measured in leading zero bits.

specs.title: NIP-14: Subject tag in text events
specs.summary: The subject tag, which gives a note a heading the way an email has one.

specs.title: NIP-15: Nostr Marketplace (for resilient marketplaces)
specs.summary: A marketplace protocol built from stalls, products and order messages, kept for the clients that implemented it.

specs.title: NIP-17: Private Direct Messages
specs.summary: Private direct messages, built from NIP-44 encryption and NIP-59 gift wraps, where the set of participants is what defines a room.

specs.title: NIP-18: Reposts
specs.summary: Kind 6, the repost, which carries the reposted note in its content and points at it with an e tag.

specs.title: NIP-19: bech32-encoded entities
specs.summary: The bech32 forms of keys, ids and pointers: npub, nsec, note, nprofile, nevent and naddr.

specs.title: NIP-21: `nostr:` URI scheme
specs.summary: The nostr: URI scheme, which turns a NIP-19 entity into a link any client can open.

specs.title: NIP-22: Comment
specs.summary: Kind 1111, the comment: a reply scoped to a root event or to an external identifier, with uppercase tags for the root and lowercase ones for the parent.

specs.title: NIP-23: Long-form Content
specs.summary: Kind 30023, long-form articles written in Markdown, addressable so their author can revise them in place.

specs.title: NIP-24: Extra metadata fields and tags
specs.summary: The fields and tags that became conventions without a NIP of their own, from display_name to the alt tag.

specs.title: NIP-25: Reactions
specs.summary: Kind 7, the reaction, whose content is a plus, a minus or an emoji, pointing at the event it answers.

specs.title: NIP-26: Delegated Event Signing
specs.summary: The delegation tag, which let one key authorise another to sign events on its behalf.

specs.title: NIP-27: Text Note References
specs.summary: How to write a mention inside content: a nostr: URI in the text, and nothing else demanded of the reader.

specs.title: NIP-28: Public Chat
specs.summary: Kinds 40 to 44, public chat channels with moderation left to the client.

specs.title: NIP-29: Relay-based Groups
specs.summary: Groups whose membership and rules are enforced by the relay hosting them, identified by an id scoped to that relay.

specs.title: NIP-30: Custom Emoji
specs.summary: The emoji tag, which maps a shortcode written in the content to an image URL.

specs.title: NIP-31: Dealing with Unknown Events
specs.summary: The alt tag, a plain text summary so a client that does not know a kind can still show something for it.

specs.title: NIP-32: Labeling
specs.summary: Kind 1985 and the L and l tags, which attach a namespaced label to an event, a key, or an external identifier.

specs.title: NIP-34: `git` stuff
specs.summary: Code collaboration on Nostr: repository announcements, repository state, patches, and issues.

specs.title: NIP-35: Torrents
specs.summary: Kind 2003, a torrent index carrying the info hash, the file list and the trackers needed to rebuild a magnet link.

specs.title: NIP-36: Sensitive Content
specs.summary: The content-warning tag, which asks a client to hide an event until the reader chooses to see it.

specs.title: NIP-37: Draft Events
specs.summary: Kind 31234, an encrypted draft of an unsigned event of any kind, stored on relays for its author alone.

specs.title: NIP-38: User Statuses
specs.summary: Kind 30315, a short-lived status: what someone is doing, or what they are listening to.

specs.title: NIP-39: Linking Profiles to Other Platforms
specs.summary: The i tags that claim an identity on another platform, each pointing at a proof anyone can check.

specs.title: NIP-40: Expiration Timestamp
specs.summary: The expiration tag, a timestamp after which relays and clients should treat an event as gone.

specs.title: NIP-42: Authentication of clients to relays
specs.summary: The AUTH flow, where a relay challenges a client to sign an ephemeral event before granting it access.

specs.title: NIP-43: Relay Access Metadata and Requests
specs.summary: How a relay advertises the roles it grants and the membership it enforces, and how a client asks to be admitted.

specs.title: NIP-44: Encrypted Payloads (Versioned)
specs.summary: The versioned encryption format the rest of Nostr builds on: secp256k1 ECDH, HKDF, padding, ChaCha20 and HMAC-SHA256.

specs.title: NIP-45: Counting results
specs.summary: The COUNT verb, which asks a relay how many events match a filter instead of asking for the events themselves.

specs.title: NIP-46: Nostr Remote Signing
specs.summary: Remote signing: a client sends signing requests over an encrypted channel to a signer that holds the key and never surrenders it.

specs.title: NIP-47: Nostr Wallet Connect
specs.summary: Nostr Wallet Connect, where a client drives a remote Lightning wallet through encrypted events.

specs.title: NIP-48: Bridged Events
specs.summary: The proxy tag, which links an event bridged from another protocol back to the object it came from.

specs.title: NIP-49: Private Key Encryption (`ncryptsec`)
specs.summary: ncryptsec, a private key encrypted under a password, with scrypt deciding how expensive guessing it is.

specs.title: NIP-50: Search Capability
specs.summary: The search field on a filter, and what a relay is expected to make of it.

specs.title: NIP-51: Lists
specs.summary: The list kinds, with public entries in the tags and private ones encrypted in the content: mutes, bookmarks, relay sets, follow sets and the rest.

specs.title: NIP-52: Calendar Events
specs.summary: Calendar events, date-based and time-based, and the RSVPs that answer them.

specs.title: NIP-53: Live Streaming and Spaces
specs.summary: Kind 30311, a live stream or audio space, rewritten as participants join and leave it.

specs.title: NIP-54: Wiki
specs.summary: Kind 30818, wiki articles addressed by a normalised subject, where several people are expected to write about the same one.

specs.title: NIP-55: Android Signer Application
specs.summary: How a client on Android asks a signer application on the same device to sign, so it never handles the private key.

specs.title: NIP-56: Reporting
specs.summary: Kind 1984, a report naming content or a key as objectionable, with a type such as nudity, malware or impersonation.

specs.title: NIP-57: Lightning Zaps
specs.summary: Zaps: the kind 9734 request a payer signs, and the kind 9735 receipt the recipient's wallet publishes once the invoice is paid.

specs.title: NIP-58: Badges
specs.summary: Badges: the definition an issuer publishes, the award it grants to a key, and the list a user chooses to show on their profile.

specs.title: NIP-59: Gift Wrap
specs.summary: Gift wraps: a rumor sealed to its recipient, then wrapped again under a throwaway key, so relays see only the wrapper.

specs.title: NIP-5A: Static Websites (nsites)
specs.summary: Static websites whose files are Blossom blobs, listed by a manifest event: one root site per key, and named sites beside it.

specs.title: NIP-60: Cashu Wallet
specs.summary: A Cashu wallet whose proofs and spending history live encrypted on relays, so it follows its owner between clients.

specs.title: NIP-61: Nutzaps
specs.summary: Nutzaps, where the payment is a Cashu token locked to the recipient's key and published to their relays, so the token itself is the receipt.

specs.title: NIP-62: Request to Vanish
specs.summary: Kind 62, a request that a relay delete everything a key ever published there.

specs.title: NIP-64: Chess (PGN)
specs.summary: Kind 64, a chess game written in PGN.

specs.title: NIP-65: Relay List Metadata
specs.summary: Kind 10002, the list saying where a key writes and where it reads mentions, which is what the outbox model is built on.

specs.title: NIP-66: Relay Discovery and Liveness Monitoring
specs.summary: Kind 30166, relay discovery events published by monitors, describing what a relay claims to be and whether it answers.

specs.title: NIP-67: EOSE Completeness Hint
specs.summary: A third element on EOSE, telling a client whether the relay really sent every stored event matching the filter.

specs.title: NIP-68: Picture-first feeds
specs.summary: Kind 20, picture-first posts where the images carry the event rather than illustrate it.

specs.title: NIP-69: Peer-to-peer Order events
specs.summary: Kind 38383, peer-to-peer trade orders shared across platforms so that their separate liquidity pools into one.

specs.title: NIP-70: Protected Events
specs.summary: The dash tag, marking an event that only its author may publish, which relays enforce through NIP-42.

specs.title: NIP-71: Video Events
specs.summary: Video events, long and short, carrying the metadata a video client needs around media hosted elsewhere.

specs.title: NIP-72: Moderated Communities
specs.summary: Kind 34550, Reddit-style communities where moderators approve the posts addressed to them.

specs.title: NIP-73: External Content IDs
specs.summary: The i tags for identifiers that exist outside Nostr: URLs, ISBNs, podcast GUIDs, DOIs, hashtags and blockchain transactions.

specs.title: NIP-75: Zap Goals
specs.summary: Kind 9041, a fundraising goal that zaps are tallied against.

specs.title: NIP-77: Negentropy Syncing
specs.summary: Negentropy over Nostr: range-based set reconciliation, so two sides transfer only the events one of them lacks.

specs.title: NIP-78: Application-specific data
specs.summary: Kind 30078, where an application stores data it has no intention of sharing with any other.

specs.title: NIP-7D: Forum Threads
specs.summary: Kind 11, a forum thread with a title, whose replies are NIP-22 comments rather than nested notes.

specs.title: NIP-84: Highlights
specs.summary: Kind 9802, a highlight: the passage someone found worth keeping, pointing back at the event or the URL it was taken from.

specs.title: NIP-85: Trusted Assertions
specs.summary: Assertions a trusted provider publishes about a key, an event or an external identifier, so a client does not have to compute a web of trust itself.

specs.title: NIP-86: Relay Management API
specs.summary: A JSON-RPC API over HTTP for administering a relay: banning keys, allowing kinds, listing what it refuses.

specs.title: NIP-87: Cashu and Fedimint Discoverability
specs.summary: How an ecash mint announces itself and its capabilities, and how users recommend the mints they trust.

specs.title: NIP-88: Polls
specs.summary: Kind 1068, a poll with its options, its type and its deadline, answered on the relays it names.

specs.title: NIP-89: Recommended Application Handlers
specs.summary: How an application declares the event kinds it can handle, and how users recommend one for a kind their client cannot open.

specs.title: NIP-90: Data Vending Machines
specs.summary: Data vending machines: paid jobs requested and delivered as events, reserving the kind range 5000 to 7000.

specs.title: NIP-92: Media Attachments Metadata (`imeta`)
specs.summary: The imeta tag, which describes a media URL found in the content: its dimensions, its mime type, its hash and its fallbacks.

specs.title: NIP-94: File Metadata
specs.summary: Kind 1063, file metadata: the url, the hash, the mime type and the size of a shared file.

specs.title: NIP-96: HTTP File Storage Integration
specs.summary: An HTTP file storage API discovered through a well-known document, replaced by Blossom.

specs.title: NIP-98: HTTP Auth
specs.summary: Kind 27235, an ephemeral event signed to authorise a single HTTP request.

specs.title: NIP-99: Classified Listings
specs.summary: Kind 30402, a classified listing: something for sale or on offer, with enough structure to be worth querying.

specs.title: NIP-A0: Voice Messages
specs.summary: Kinds 1222 and 1244, short voice messages whose content is the URL of an audio file.

specs.title: NIP-A4: Public Messages
specs.summary: Kind 24, a plain text message addressed to one or more keys, meant for a notification screen rather than a thread.

specs.title: NIP-B0: Web Bookmarks
specs.summary: Kind 39701, a web bookmark addressed by its own URI, editable by whoever saved it.

specs.title: NIP-B7: Blossom
specs.summary: How a Nostr client uses Blossom for media: reading a user's server list, and uploading to the servers it names.

specs.title: NIP-BE: Nostr BLE Communications Protocol
specs.summary: How two devices speak Nostr over Bluetooth Low Energy, emulating the websocket protocol within its limits.

specs.title: NIP-C0: Code Snippets
specs.summary: Kind 1337, a code snippet carrying its language, its filename, its extension and its runtime.

specs.title: NIP-C7: Chats
specs.summary: Kind 9, a chat message, whose replies are further kind 9 events quoting their parent.

specs.title: NIP-CC: Geocaching
specs.summary: Kind 37516 and its companions, geocache listings and the logs of the people who found them.

specs.title: NIP-EE: E2EE Messaging using MLS Protocol
specs.summary: End-to-end encrypted group messaging built on the MLS protocol, superseded by Marmot.

specs.title: NIP-F4: Podcasts
specs.summary: Podcast episodes published as events, so a feed stops depending on one URL staying alive.
